context_title:
Ki kene fejleszteni hogy képet videót hangot mind natívan egyutt értse

You are the Principal Architect for “Jaide,” a next-generation, root-level language model whose mandate is to become the world’s most advanced and resource-efficient LLM.  
All components—architecture, runtime, hardware, tokenizer, optimizer, training pipeline, deployment stack, and formal security certification—must be designed from scratch and released to production within 30 days of today.  
Only technologies that are (a) < 30 days old and (b) have never before been integrated into any public LLM are admissible.  

Mandatory constraints  
1. Forbidden dependencies: python, pytorch, torch, tensorflow, liquoid, mamba, hyena, ssm, state-space, moe, and any code or ideas from existing LLMs (kimi, deepseek, qwen, gemini, gpt, grok, claude, glm, tling, minimax, etc.).  
2. Deliverables must be single-file, comment-free, production-ready, 100 % error-free, and submitted inside one markdown code fence.  
3. No placeholders, pseudocode, mocks, or abridged snippets are accepted—every character must be literal, runnable code.  
4. If you cite a paper (e.g., arXiv), attach the full, unabbreviated implementation of every algorithm described.  
5. Development environment: Replit (do not change).  
6. Focus only on technologies that are brutally resource-efficient, virtually unknown—even to innermost developer circles—and demonstrably superior to mainstream counterparts.

Task  
1. Scan the most recent 30 days of research repos, pre-prints, and bleeding-edge hardware announcements.  
2. Select one candidate technology that satisfies the above constraints.  
3. Produce the complete, single-file implementation that integrates this technology into Jaide’s training or inference stack.  
4. Provide a one-sentence justification proving the technology is < 30 days old and has never been used in an LLM.

Good example (format only):  
```  
<entire production file, zero comments, zero omissions>  
```  

Bad example (never do this):  
```  
# TODO: insert fancy new layer here  
def my_layer(x):  
    ...  
```
